title: Populate the scheduler feature barrel (scheduler.dart) with real exports

evidence.quote: // feature. Do NOT import deep paths directly.

why: The entire file is a library declaration plus a comment claiming to be the feature's public surface — it contains zero `export` statements, so importing it gives a consumer nothing usable. Grepping the whole repo confirms no file anywhere imports `features/scheduler/scheduler.dart`; every cross-feature consumer (e.g. lib/core/labels/curriculum_label.dart, lib/core/providers/calendar_providers.dart) is forced into deep imports of internal scheduler files because there is nothing else to import. The same empty-barrel pattern exists in learning.dart and profiles.dart and settings.dart (0 exports each) versus tracks.dart (26 exports, a real barrel) — so Rule 2 is currently unimplementable for scheduler even by a well-intentioned contributor, independent of the separate checker bug (see the awk finding).
recommendation: Either populate scheduler.dart with `export` statements for the types/providers other features legitimately need (services, providers, models used cross-feature) and migrate the deep-import call sites, or formally scope down Rule 2's claim until barrels are built out feature-by-feature.
acceptance_criteria: scheduler.dart exports the symbols currently deep-imported by other features (calendar_program_service.dart, local_calendar_engine.dart, learning_program_service.dart, calendar_program_registry.dart at minimum).
Once check 15 (see companion finding) is fixed, a grep for `features/scheduler/(?!scheduler\.dart)` from outside lib/features/scheduler/ returns zero matches.

corrections: coding-standards.md lines 80/82/84/744 literally name the barrel 'providers.dart', not '<feature>.dart' — a doc/tooling drift the finding doesn't flag. Also, check-15's awk logic (Makefile lines 374-385) is tautologically broken (always compares a file's own feature name to itself), so the digest's '~32 known baselined edges' is entirely check-14/Rule-1 content, not check-15/Rule-2 — this reinforces rather than undermines the finding's novelty.
